title: Trust your gut, check the habits
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When you needed someone badly, did you ignore a feeling about them?

A student said: the topic is so key. You need to be able to listen to your gut. Sometimes we approach things out of need: we haven't found an engineer for six months and this is the only guy I'm interviewing. But you know that person is not fit for your team.

You already understand how your people perform and what environment they feel comfortable in, the student said. When you bring in a disruption, it leads to a worse case for you to deal with. Don't skip the gut feeling because you are stressed about getting someone.
I asked another student, with long corporate experience: how important is this profiling of character against the resume and the formal things? What percentage would you give?

The student said: very, very important, and crucial. It is not just the interview of what they have on paper. Sometimes you go a little out of the context of what the person is hired for. You develop those skills with time.
A student said: someone who is perceptive, who listens carefully to your questions, matters. Some people try to start a conflict with you from the moment you talk to them, or take over the interview.
The student added that each of us can identify someone who will bring value to the team and someone who will not. It is like a sixth sense you build.
I said I have learned a lot from living with people I work with. Are they organized or disorganized? The daily habits tell you a lot about somebody.
That is why companies do team-building events and obstacle courses, I said. What you can learn about somebody in a week outside the office is massive.
What does your gut say about the person you are about to bring in?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the last time you ignored your gut because you needed someone.
Write how much weight you give a resume against the person.
Write what you would look for in a week of shared time.
Write the habit that would tell you most.

check.q: What did a student say not to skip because you are stressed?
What did I say tells you a lot about somebody?
What did I say team-building events show?
choices: What you can learn about somebody outside the office

recap: Listen to your gut, and check the habits. Don't hire out of need alone.
